## Decided against

Kept rather than deleted: the reasoning is the useful part.

- [FE-34](./items/FE-34.md) — First unproved bridge as a general requirement. Falsified by the second adopter. RH's contracts C1-C8 are chains, so each has an earliest unestablished link. PvsNP has no equivalent concept and dropped a sequential ordering rule on its own record as wrong: its lower-bound tracks import only the clause and counting layers, use no Turing machine, and serialising them behind Cook-Levin would have bought nothing and cost the two closures that came out of running them.
- [FE-35](./items/FE-35.md) — Ledger-reconciliation significance signals. Three of the four candidate signals are falsified by measurement. 781 of 987 declarations are named somewhere in prose, but 799 of 970 appear only in log documents and the three most important synthesis documents name zero — so the signal selects nearly everything and its negation selects the wrong things. Exported-versus-internal fails identically in a library organised by namespace. Dependency-reachability inherits the chain assumption rejected in FE-34.
- [FE-36](./items/FE-36.md) — More detectors, to raise frameworkCoverage. 53 of 82 is not an optimization target, and both trials strengthened the case rather than weakening it: the framework's two genuine findings both came from manual judgement, and its most serious failures both came from automated detectors.
- [FE-37](./items/FE-37.md) — More standards beyond the 22. The 22 cover the source prompt and the charter. Neither adopter asked for a 23rd; both asked for existing rules to work.
- [FE-38](./items/FE-38.md) — Network-backed citation checking. RH's two citation rules were the ones it could not review, and the obstacle is having the papers, not resolving the identifiers. Both adopters recorded declining rather than guessing.
- [FE-39](./items/FE-39.md) — A profile mechanism. Applicability already tailors per rule. §0k asks for a third value, not a bundle.
